Node.js

Run server-side APIs and integration logic in JavaScript.

NOfficial product ↗Open in the hierarchy →
Level 4Inspect the detail

Node.js runs JavaScript outside the browser and can support APIs, integration services, and development tooling. We can use it for the server side of a customer portal, webhook receiver, or workflow service. The design separates validation, permissions, and business logic from the interface so a team can inspect failures and maintain integrations without relying on manual work.

Useful outputs

  • Validated API or integration service
  • Structured logging and failure responses
  • Run configuration and maintenance notes

Where we can apply it

  • Lead ingestion: webhook → validation → deduplication → CRM update.
  • Payment status: signed event → business state update → customer notification.
  • Data connector: source API → normalized fields → reporting database.
01

Use case 1

Receive lead or payment webhooks and update authorized business records.

02

Use case 2

Create API endpoints for a customer portal or internal tool.

03

Use case 3

Build small integration services that normalize data between platforms.

Inputs we need

  • Endpoint contracts and expected event samples
  • Authentication and database requirements
  • Hosting, logging, and traffic assumptions

Delivery sequence

  • Define routes, permissions, and expected request and response shapes.
  • Implement business logic with validation, idempotency, and useful errors.
  • Test representative failures and deploy with suitable health monitoring.

Expert review points

  • Review authorization and input validation at every endpoint.
  • Confirm event retries cannot duplicate payments or record changes.

We confirm available integrations, plans, permissions, and data mapping before implementing these connection candidates.

  • API error rate
